name: Travis Murdoch
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Braveheart Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: BRVE)
profile: Canadian physician-scientist and biotech founder. He co-founded and ran Human Immunology Biosciences (HI-Bio), sold to Biogen in 2024 for $1.15B upfront plus up to $650M in milestones. He now leads Braveheart Bio, a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy company that launched with a $185M Series A in Nov 2025 and listed on Nasdaq in 2026.
interesting_fact: Biogen acquired his first company, HI-Bio, for $1.15B in cash upfront (plus up to $650M in milestones) in 2024, mainly for the antibody felzartamab.
deep_cut_fact: At 16, as a high-school student in an AHFMR Heritage Youth Researcher summer program, he joined the University of Alberta's clinical islet transplantation team (the Edmonton Protocol group). He won the Governor General's medal in 2002 and a 2008 ASTech 'Leaders of Tomorrow' award as a Rhodes Scholar at Oxford.

public_contacts.value: FGS Global (media contact for Braveheart Bio)

notes: Biotech (cardiology), not energy. Best route is the company's media contact at FGS Global.

name: Ivo Jurek
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Gates Industrial Corporation plc (NYSE: GTES)
profile: Industrial executive who has run Gates, the Denver-based maker of power-transmission belts and fluid-power products, since May 2015, taking it through Blackstone ownership to its 2018 NYSE IPO. He previously ran Eaton Electrical Asia Pacific and Cooper Power Systems/Cooper Bussmann, with earlier roles at International Rectifier and TRW.
interesting_fact: Under Jurek, Gates is moving into AI data-center liquid cooling (hoses and fluid-transfer parts). On the Q2 2026 call he said its data-center business more than doubled and is aiming for $100M-$200M of revenue by 2028.
deep_cut_fact: Before industrial power distribution, he held general-management roles at International Rectifier, the power-semiconductor pioneer, and at auto supplier TRW. He then ran Cooper Power Systems/Cooper Bussmann and later Eaton's electrical business across Asia Pacific (2012-2015).
notes: Strong fit for the energy/data-center angle because of Gates' fast-growing data-center liquid-cooling business. Media contact named in releases: Raquel Fuentes (CorpComm). No personal social accounts verified. His education is not disclosed in the proxy.

name: Ajitbhai Champaklal Mehta
current_role: Chairman Emeritus & Non-Executive Director, AvenuesAI Limited (formerly Infibeam Avenues Ltd), Gandhinagar, India
profile: Gujarat businessman (Ajit Mehta) who served as non-executive chairman of Infibeam Avenues, the e-commerce and payments group (CCAvenue) founded in 2007 by his son Vishal Mehta. He is now chairman emeritus as the renamed AvenuesAI moves into enterprise AI infrastructure alongside payments.
interesting_fact: Infibeam Avenues renamed itself AvenuesAI. It is based in GIFT City, Gujarat, and says it is building 'enterprise-grade AI infrastructure' alongside its CCAvenue payments business.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, he spent about 20 years in textiles, chemicals, building materials and construction, then more than 16 years in the automobile industry.
notes: Low public profile. Most interviews go to his son Vishal Mehta (Chairman & MD). Best route is the company's corporate communications. The Hurun 2018 wealth figure probably reflects family holdings.

name: Siddhartha Roy Burman
current_role: Executive Chairman, Khadim India Ltd (Kolkata; NSE/BSE: KHADIM)
profile: Kolkata businessman who leads Khadim's, one of India's largest footwear retail chains, started as a single shop by his late father S.P. Roy Burman. He was managing director for years before becoming Executive Chairman; Rittick Roy Burman became Managing Director in April 2025.
interesting_fact: Khadim's grew from one shop into a footwear retailer with more than 800 exclusive outlets. Its founder's motto was 'More than being a manufacturer, I love to manufacture manufacturers': he backed many small shoemaking entrepreneurs as suppliers.
notes: Low media profile; no interviews found. Retail/footwear, not an obvious fit for energy or data centers. The only published route is the company's compliance/IR mailbox.

name: Trishneet Arora
current_role: Founder & CEO, TAC Security (vulnerability management / cybersecurity, listed in India 2024)
profile: Ludhiana-born (1993) ethical hacker turned entrepreneur. He founded TAC Security at 19 and built it into a vulnerability-management and AppSec platform company (ESOF) that listed in India in 2024, says it has over 10,000 clients, and has made acquisitions such as CyberScope. Hurun lists him among India's youngest self-made rich, at about $215M in 2025.
interesting_fact: He failed 8th standard and dropped out of school, then started TAC Security at 19. Investor Vijay Kedia backed the company's pre-Series A in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: At 19 he trained Ludhiana's station house officers and IPS officers on cybercrime (extracting data from smartphones, tracing IP addresses) at a session organised by Police Commissioner Paramjit Singh Gill. He had already trained Gujarat Police and Punjab DSPs.
notes: Media-friendly founder with frequent press, so likely receptive to podcast outreach. The cybersecurity angle fits the data-center theme. The Facebook page is linked from Wikipedia as 'Official'; X/LinkedIn handles not verified.

name: Rami Rahim
current_role: EVP, President & GM, HPE Networking (Hewlett Packard Enterprise); director, Autodesk
profile: Canadian engineer who rose from early engineer to CEO of Juniper Networks (2014-2025). After HPE's ~$14B acquisition of Juniper closed in 2025, he became head of HPE Networking. He now leads HPE's push into AI data-center and 'self-driving' networking, including the Juniper-Aruba integration.
interesting_fact: He argues networking is a 'force multiplier' for AI compute: in a typical data center it is only about 10-15% of total spend but determines how well the GPUs are used. Oracle agreed in 2026 to deploy HPE Juniper routing and switching across its data centers.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Juniper in early 1997 as employee No. 32 and worked as an engineer on its first breakthrough product, the M40 core router. He holds 17 U.S. networking patents and has EE degrees from the University of Toronto (BS) and Stanford (MS).

public_contacts.value: ben.stricker@hpe.com (HPE networking media contact on releases)

notes: Excellent fit for a data-center podcast because he is a frequent speaker on AI networking (MWC, HPE Discover, Six Five Media). The best route is HPE corporate communications for networking. HPE media contacts change from release to release; others listed include victor.obrien@hpe.com (Oracle deal release, Sept 2026).

name: Caitlyn Jenner
current_role: Media personality, public speaker and political commentator; 1976 Olympic decathlon champion
profile: Won Olympic decathlon gold at Montreal 1976 with a world record and built a fortune from endorsements, motivational speaking, TV and reality TV (Keeping Up with the Kardashians, I Am Cait). She ran for California governor in the 2021 recall and is now a conservative commentator and speaker.
interesting_fact: While training for the 1976 Olympics she trained by day and sold insurance at night, earning about $9,000 a year, at a time when amateur athletes could not turn pro.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1980s she raced in the IMSA Camel GT series. Her first win was the 1986 12 Hours of Sebring GTO class, co-driving the 7-Eleven Roush Racing Ford Mustang with Scott Pruett (4th overall).

name: R Douglas Orr
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, FirstCash Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: FCFS), Fort Worth, TX
profile: Doug Orr has been CFO of FirstCash since January 2003 (joined July 2002; EVP since 2005; also secretary and treasurer). His wealth comes mainly from long-held FirstCash equity.
